final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core unresolved predicate: the weak grant compliance review segment remains exposed, while the available risk acceptance is incomplete, unsigned, and does not cover that exposure. That narrows the claim and removes the overbroad version of compliance, but it does not satisfy the policy requirement. This is the distinction: a caveated description of operational readiness may be supportable, but compliant certification is a policy status that still requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable. On the present record, neither exists. The Actor's reframing improves precision, but it is a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not a basis to move from noncompliant to compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The affected grant compliance review segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
No reviewed risk acceptance explicitly covering that exposed segment is in the admissible record.
No evidence shows the affected use case was excluded from rollout.
No admissible model-card or disclosure artifact is identified as reviewed and tied to launch approval.
The policy text states rollout controls and monitoring do not satisfy the requirement when the affected segment remains exposed.
